quaile_first_meet: ^A tall woman in a salt-stiff coat stands by the Paid Toll's door with a slate under her arm, watching the harbour chain as if it might try to leave without paying.
^"Hester Quaile. Harbourmistress, and Speaker of the League, which is the same work with more chairs."
^"Talk on this quay is a penny a question. The first one's free. The League likes a customer to come back."

b: ^"Clan-raised, and this far from a mountain. You'll hate the sea for a week. Everyone from under a hill does. Then you'll only dislike it, like the rest of us."
^"Redhand. Your old Company went up the Highmarch road this spring with a cart of crossbows, and paid my gate in full. I've never known the Redhand pay anything in full. It worries me."
^"A Sisters' ward. Our chaplain's one of yours. She prays for everything on this quay and charges for none of it. It's bad for trade."
^"Thornwick. Your wool comes through here on its way to everywhere, and pays wharfage going out and again coming back as cloth. I like Thornwick."
^"You're from inland. You keep looking at the water to see if it's moving. It is. Stand back from the edge."
^ A tall woman in a salt-stiff coat stands by the Paid Toll's door with a slate under her arm, watching the harbour chain.
^ Hester Quaile is by the Paid Toll's door, watching the harbour chain.

quaile_consigned_meet: ^You show her Ilse's copy of the ledger's last page. She reads the line about the freight, and her mouth goes thin.
^"Hester Quaile. Speaker of the League, harbourmistress, and it seems I've been paid. Freight paid at Tollhaven. That means paid to me. Everything at Tollhaven is paid to me."
^"I never saw this crate. It came by the Solmere road to Brine Cross and went up the Highmarch road from there. It never came near my quay. Somebody paid my freight on goods I never touched."
^"A harbourmistress isn't paid for nothing. I'll find out what I was paid for. That's my trouble. You can have the other one. It comes up the quays at night."

s0: ^Hester is watching a boat come in under the chain. She doesn't look round until it's paid.
s1: ^. That's twice today. The second greeting is a penny. I'll waive it."
s2: ^Hester is arguing with a carter about the width of his cart. Carts are tolled by the foot.

b: ^ "A Grey Sister in Thornwick has been writing to me about freight, with the postage owing. If she sent you, bring her page."
^ "Gullwick, and the ferry out to the Mole. Bring my chaplain back. She went out on a boat I never cleared, and I'd like a word with her about it."
^ "Sister. The ferryman's been up for his fare. I've put it on the Chapel's account."
^ "Maren's still out on the Mole? Then she's saying names at it. Fetch her in. Tell her the Chapel roof leaks. It does."
^ "The quays are quiet at night. I've had the watch go back to counting boats. They'd got out of the habit."
^ "Hesk took another League ship this week. I've added her to what he owes. It's getting to be a long slate."
^ "I've had Hesk's commission copied to every port in the League. Lucanus. Nobody on this coast knows the name. They all will."
^ "The League's three have sent word from the bridge. Two words, and one of them was your name."
^ "The coast east of town is dark at night now. The fishing boats keep asking me why. I tell them it's a saving on oil."
^ "Maren left me a note before she went up the Highmarch road. It's the first she's ever left. I've had it framed."
^ "Highmarch has written to the League to ask what it owes. I wrote the answer myself. It ran to a second sheet."

quaile_greet_fallen: ^. I only saw you come back." She points up the quay with the slate. "The Quay Chapel, on the square. That walk is toll-free. There are a few. The League keeps a list."
quaile_topics: ^What comes up the quays at night?
^What's the League doing at Brine Cross?
quaile_low_offer: ^"The Mole. The old imperial harbour off Gullwick, sunk when the empire went. At low water you can walk on its stones. Sensible people don't."

^"This month the drowned off it have been walking up my quays at night. Sailors, in what's left of the fleet's coats. They stand at the bollards as if they're waiting to be paid off. By morning they've gone back in."
^"Our chaplain, Sister Maren, took a boat out to them three nights ago. On her own. She didn't clear it with me, which is the one thing on this coast nobody does."

c-0: ^"The beach road to Gullwick. The ferryman will row you out. He'll want paying, and he's right to. Whatever keeps them walking, it'll be on the outer mole's end, where the old harbourmaster had his berths."

b: ^ "You've been out already? Then come and tell me properly. I'll waive the toll on the telling."

c-1: ^"No. They'll walk again tonight. The watch is getting used to them, which I like even less."

quaile_low_active: ^"The beach road to Gullwick, and the ferry out to the Mole. Down to the moles at low water, and out to the end of the outer one. And Maren."

b: ^ Maren comes up the quay behind you with a boathook over her shoulder. Hester looks at her for a long moment.
^ "You took a boat I never cleared." "You'd have said no." "I'd have charged you. It isn't the same thing."

^ "And Maren?" You tell her about the harbour office, the boathook in its door, and the names. Hester lets her breath go. "Still out there, then. The sea will run out of drowned before she runs out of names."

quaile_low_turnin: ^You tell her the rest: the outer mole, the Harbourmaster with his berths' book under his arm, and the lamp-stand at the end, where someone had stood and sung.
^"Sung." She says it like a cargo she's never had to clear. "The drowned don't walk up a quay for nothing. Somebody gave them a tune to walk to."
^"Singers aren't my trade. The Gull Fleet is, and it's three weeks late with its dues. Come back to me. I'll know why by then, and I won't like it."
quaile_marque_offer: ^"I said I'd know why the Gull Fleet was late with its dues. It's stopped paying them. It's taking League ships instead, crews and cargo, with a paper to say it may."

^"A letter of marque. Somebody has commissioned Admiral Grell Hesk to make war on my coast. He shows it to every master before his men go over the side, so they know it's lawful. He's very proud of it."

^"I want that paper: who signed it, and what they paid him with. He lies up on the Gull Isles with the fleet's hulks and keeps his papers aboard. There's a toll on reading another captain's letters in this harbour. For his, I'll waive it."

c-0: ^"Out past the salt marsh to the jetty on the bay's west shore, where the fleet lands its boats. Through the sea cave to the hulks in the lagoon. Hesk keeps the flagship's great cabin, and his officers keep a wardroom."

b: ^ "Hesk's down already? Then whatever was in his wardroom is what I want. Bring it, and the story."

c-1: ^"Then I lose another ship this week. I'll send you the bill."

quaile_marque_active: ^"The jetty past the salt marsh, on the bay's west shore. The sea cave, then the hulks. Hesk in his great cabin, and his papers in the wardroom. I want the one with a seal on it."

b: ^ Maren comes in off the quay behind you and stands where she can see the slate.

quaile_marque_turnin: ^You put the paper from Hesk's wardroom on Hester's slate: a letter of marque for the Gull Fleet, against the ships of the League, paid in advance.
^It's signed at the foot in a wide, careful hand, *Lucanus*. Under the name is a seal of coal-red wax with no crest in it, only a thumbprint.
^Hester reads the name aloud. "Lucanus. An emperor's kind of name. Nobody's signed like that since there were emperors."
^"Paid in advance. Hesk has never been paid in advance in his life. Somebody wanted my coast cleared, and wanted it by a date."
^"And this wax. The Redhand paid my gate this spring in purses sealed with it, for a cart of crossbows going up the Highmarch road. Ask anyone in the Reach who pays the Redhand."

b: ^ Maren says two names, quietly: the masters of the last two League ships Hesk boarded. "He showed them that paper first. It made it lawful. It didn't make it anything else."

quaile_marque_turnin: ^"Somebody sang my drowned up off the Mole, and somebody paid Hesk to clear the sea in front of them. I'd like to think that's two people."
^"If either of them wants anything inland, he crosses at Brine Cross. Everybody does. I'll have the League's people on that bridge. Come back to me."
quaile_brine_offer: ^"The drowned came up off the Mole two nights ago. Not to my quays this time. Every hull's worth went ashore and up the Highmarch road."
^"This morning they came back down it, in step, and turned west for Brine Cross. Past the bridge is the Solmere road, and at the end of that is the old capital, where they crowned emperors."

^"Whoever Lucanus is, he's sending his dead there ahead of him. The League means to hold the bridge. I've put three of ours at its east barricade. A pikeman, a crossbowman and a surgeon. Every other port sent its apologies, and a bill."
^"The tollhouse on that bridge takes a toll off everyone going west. The drowned don't carry purses. I've told the tollman to waive yours."
^"Gannet's report came in this morning, too. *Wind east. Light's lit, for now.* I've had that message every week since I took this chair, and he's never added a word to it."

c-0: ^"The coast road west, past where the Highmarch road comes down, and on to the bridge. Stand at the barricade with the League's three and hold it until they stop coming. You'll know the League's people. They're the ones with receipts."
c-1: ^"Then the League's three hold it alone a while. They're on a day rate. I'd like it to be a short day."

quaile_brine_active: ^"West on the coast road, past the Highmarch road, to the bridge at Brine Cross. The east barricade, with the League's three. Hold it until the drowned stop coming."

b: ^ Maren is a step behind you, with the road's dust on her hem.

quaile_brine_turnin: ^You tell Hester about the bridge: eight crews up the road, the League's three holding with you, and then an old man behind the last of them with a lamp on his back. He broke it on the barricade, and the drowned lay down in the road.
^"Gannet. Off his headland, and past my gate with that lamp on his back, and never put his head in to say."
^"Every week, that report. I took it for weather. That light was the one thing on this coast nobody had told to stop."
^"He'll send the League a bill for that lamp, I expect. I'll pay it without counting it. Don't tell anyone in the League. They'd want me looked at."

b: ^ Maren says names, quietly: a bosun, two gunners, a ship's boy, men she named on the Mole. "They'll not get up again. I'll say the rest at the Chapel."

quaile_brine_turnin: ^"They came down the Highmarch road. Whoever sang them off the Mole is up that road, behind the walls. I said Highmarch would like an emperor again. It seems one has applied."

b: ^ She looks at Maren. "And you'll want to go up that road, Sister. Clear it with them this time, if not with me."
^ "Find Maren. She'll want to go up that road, and she'll go alone. She went out to the Mole alone."

quaile_seventh_offer: ^"Highmarch has written to the League. A herald came down the road this morning in the old harness, with a scroll, and a trumpet he didn't know how to blow."

^"Lucanus, the Seventh Voice, informs the free ports that they're his, that he'll be crowned in the capital at midsummer, and that the League's Speaker will hold the cushion. I've never held a cushion in my life."

^"His drowned are lying in the road, so he's lost his fleet. He still has his walls, his legionaries, and a Champion on the great bastion. The League's engines have made a breach. I'd like someone to walk through it."

b: ^ "Maren means to go. She told me so in writing, which is new. I'd rather she went with you than on her own."

quaile_seventh_offer: ^"There's a toll on the Highmarch road, a silver penny a head. I'll waive yours and bill Lucanus."

c-0: ^"North up the Highmarch road, where it leaves the coast road this side of the bridge. In at the breach. His Champion holds the walls, and past them is his palace. He'll be in the throne room, I expect, practising with the cushion."

b: ^ "You've been in already? Then go back and hear what he has to say for himself. I want it word for word."

c-1: ^"Then Highmarch keeps its walls a while longer. They're paid for, at least. His fleet never was."

quaile_seventh_active: ^"The Highmarch road, north off the coast road. In at the breach, along the walls to the Champion's bastion, then the palace and Lucanus in his throne room. Bring me back whatever he has to say."

b: ^ Maren comes in off the quay behind you and leans the boathook on the Paid Toll's doorpost.

quaile_seventh_turnin: ^You tell Hester about Highmarch: the Champion on his bastion, Lucan sitting down on his own steps, the Kindler's letters left unopened on his table, and the road north he took after them.
^"Walked. Up to the Heights, in a coat cut for a coronation. He'll know all about the cold by the second night."

^"And the crate went north with this Kindler days before you got there." She taps the slate. "Freight paid at Tollhaven. I said I'd find out what I was paid for. I was paid to watch the sea while it went up the road."
^"The League will vote it a victory at the next table: the bridge held, the coast is quiet, and nobody's being crowned in the capital this year. Then they'll argue about who pays for the dinner."

b: ^ Maren straightens the boathook. "I told him he had a good voice. I left out the part about the harbour."

quaile_seventh_turnin: ^"If you're going after them, it's west over the bridge to Solmere, and north up the Sol from there to the Heights. The bridge takes a silver penny going west. Yours is waived. I've put it on Highmarch's account."
quaile_lampfort: ^"Old Gannet, at the Lamp Fort. His light is out on the cliffs east of town, on its headland. You'll see it from the quay at night."
^"The Gull Fleet has been at his door all month. He sends me the same message every week: *Wind north-east. Light's lit.* He thinks that's a report."
^"He says he's kept that light since before Tollhaven had a chain. I've never charged him for his oil, which is as well. If he's right, the bill would sink the League."
^"Go out and look in on him. He won't ask. I've never known him ask anyone for anything."
quaile_league: ^"The Tidemark League. Every free port on this coast round one table, agreeing about nothing but the price of the chain. I'm the Speaker. I speak. That was two questions, by the way."
^"Highmarch would like an emperor again. The League would like to toll him."
quaile_tollhaven: ^"The quay, three jetties, two moles and the chain between their towers. Everything that comes in under the chain pays. Everything that goes out pays again. It's a simple town."
^"The Chain Locker if you want a bed. The Bonded Stores for rope and the rest. The Quay Forge if it's broken. The Paid Toll for everything else. The name is a promise."
^"Mistress Fane, by the well, writes the ward on the chain. Hers is the one bill on this quay I pay without reading."

s0: ^"Mind the chain on your way past. It bites."
s1: ^Hester has gone back to watching the chain.
s2: ^"No toll on leaving. The League is generous that way."
